evidence.text: The Cedar study trained a logistic regression classifier on the Cedar-240 dataset. The dataset contained 240 labeled records. Training used a batch size of 32 for 12 epochs. The authors reported macro F1 of 0.81 on a held-out test split. The author-reported limitation was the small sample size.

The Willow study reranked the union of lexical and dense retrieval candidates using a cross-encoder. Reciprocal rank fusion used a constant of 60. The final answer context contained six passages. The reported nDCG at 10 was 0.79 on the Willow-500 evaluation set. The authors measured quality on that dataset only, not on the Cedar or Maple datasets.

The Maple study evaluated a dense embedding retriever on the Maple-600 dataset containing 600 passages. Embeddings had 384 dimensions. The reported MRR at 10 was 0.67. Each query retrieved 20 candidates before evaluation. The authors identified vocabulary drift as a limitation.

The Birch study evaluated BM25 retrieval on the Birch-900 collection of 900 passages. The tokenizer lowercased text and retained hyphenated technical terms. The reported recall at 10 was 0.74. The authors did not evaluate multilingual queries. The collection consisted only of English laboratory reports.
